value: Gardarsdottir, S.O., De Lena, E., Romano, M., Roussanaly, S., Voldsund, M., Perez-Calvo, J.-F., Berstad, D., Fu, C., Anantharaman, R., Sutter, D., Gazzani, M., Mazzotti, M., Cinti, G. (2019). Comparison of Technologies for CO2 Capture from Cement Production - Part 2: Cost Analysis. Energies 12(3), 542. doi:10.3390/en12030542. With Supplementary Materials (equipment lists).

Region: Europe (generic EU BAT plant, EU-28 2014 power mix). Loaded: reference BAT kiln cost basis (TPC 204 M EUR, opex 41 M EUR/yr, cost of clinker 62.6 EUR/t, economic parameters); six retrofit cases as whole plants (Voldsund 2019 names, INCLUDES CAPTURE: TPC with capture, annual OPEX, cost of clinker, CAC, clinker rate, share-to-capture 90%) with per-t-clinker coal, electricity and steam flows from Table 2; and the capture plants separately (TPC of the capture plant = TPC with capture minus reference) as capture-unit rows. Costs are the paper own bottom-up estimates in EUR 2014, Nth-of-a-kind. Not loaded: SI equipment lists (component costs, kEUR 2014), figure bars (breakdown of clinker cost and CAC, read from charts), sensitivity curves (Fig. 6). Traps: (1) the PDF text layer holds a second review-draft layer (scrambled interleaved text) - Table 6 was read from the clean layer: TPC cement+capture 204/280/332/353/450/406/424, capture plant 76/128/149/247/202/220, OPEX 41/76/58/66/71/59/61, cost of clinker 62.6/107.4/93.0/104.9/120.0/105.8/110.3, CAC 80.2/42.4/66.2/83.5/52.4/58.6, all consistent (capture TPC = total minus 204); (2) Table 2 electric power is net of on-site generation for the oxyfuel and CaL cases (inferred from Voldsund Table 15; Table 2 states no sign convention); (3) coal and steam are not converted to GJ here (no heating value printed in this paper; LHV used by Part 1 and 3 and 6 EUR/GJ LHV); (4) the oxyfuel and integrated CaL capture TPC includes the kiln modifications, so a capture-unit archetype for them would double count the host; (5) the CAC excludes CO2 transport and storage.
